scope: Small primary-paper audit for at most two prospective GeoNet mechanism experiments

sources.title: TEAM-LM: Earthquake magnitude and location estimation from real time seismic waveforms with a transformer network
sources.version: arXiv v2 dated 14 April 2021, retrieved PDF has 44 pages
sources.access: Primary preprint full text accessible in web tool; publisher and GFZ PDF open attempts failed in this task
sources.checked_claim: Variable-station attention uses peak-normalized waveforms with a retained log-amplitude feature. Five-Gaussian magnitude and fifteen-Gaussian location outputs are trained separately. Chronological and inter-region experiments exist, but none reproduces this prospective GeoNet Mw cohort.

sources.title: Rapid magnitude estimation for Taiwan earthquake early warning via frequency-domain multi-station deep learning
sources.access: Publisher full HTML accessible; no author code or checkpoints downloaded/executed
sources.checked_claim: FNO features receive distance corrections, followed by an LSTM and scalar output. The trigger clock starts after the fourth P arrival. Weighted-MSE benefits for larger events are modest and not always significant, while aggregate error is comparable. This is distinct from the first-P GeoNet Mw task.

sources.title: Data-Knowledge Driven Hybrid Deep Learning for Earthquake Early Warning
sources.access: Publisher full HTML accessible, particularly methodology and distance-feature discussion
sources.checked_claim: CNN/GCN features combine with physical information including epicentral distance. Distance information improves the reported magnitude experiment; a separately predicted-distance arm supports practical inference. Magnitudes >=8 are excluded. No matched GeoNet or first-network-P 1/3/5 reproduction is inferred.

sources.title: A Bayesian Method for Real-Time Earthquake Location Using Multiparameter Data
sources.access: Primary publisher full text/search extraction accessible
sources.checked_claim: Evolving location distributions combine differential P times, amplitude ratios and backazimuth. This is direct prior art for probabilistic multi-observation source geometry, rather than proof of a new neural magnitude-tail effect.

sources.title: The Virtual Seismologist (VS) method: a Bayesian approach to earthquake early warning
sources.access: Primary author-hosted 39-page chapter PDF accessible; no local download
sources.checked_claim: Joint magnitude/location posterior estimation uses amplitude relationships and prior information, including station/site terms. The chapter discusses sparse data and long-rupture point-source limitations. Generic marginalization, source uncertainty and site correction therefore cannot be claimed new.

sources.title: Multi-events earthquake early warning algorithm using a Bayesian approach
sources.access: Author-institution primary record and abstract accessible; publisher open failed, while indexed primary publisher text was searchable. Full linked PDF was not downloaded in this task
sources.checked_claim: A Bayesian method addresses concurrent-event model selection and parameter inference. It establishes joint probabilistic EEW prior art; no magnitude-MAE numerical comparison or exact early-clock reproduction is claimed here.

literature_claim_policy: Keep paper-derived prose below200 words per web source. Proposal architectures, controls and invented linear arithmetic are agent-designed, not claimed author results. No novelty or benchmark-superiority claims.
